definitions.explanation: A person who has just joined a group, organization, or workplace.

examples.japanese: {新入|しんい}りの{社員|しゃいん}を{紹介|しょうかい}する。
{彼|かれ}はまだ{新入|しんい}りだから、わからないことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: He's still a newcomer, so there's a lot he doesn't know.

examples.japanese: {新入|しんい}りだからといって{遠慮|えんりょ}する{必要|ひつよう}はない。
examples.english: Just because you're new doesn't mean you have to hold back.

notes:
{新|しん} (new) + {入|い}り (entering). Refers to someone who has recently joined an organization or group and is still learning the ropes. The term has a slightly informal, colloquial feel and is commonly used in workplaces and clubs.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新入|しんい}りの{社員|しゃいん} — new employee
- {新入|しんい}りの{メンバー|めんばー} — new member
- {新入|しんい}りを{鍛|きた}える — train the newcomer
- {新入|しんい}りいじめ — hazing of newcomers

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {新人|しんじん} — newcomer; rookie — more formal and widely used in business and media
- {新入生|しんにゅうせい} — new student; first-year student — specifically for schools
- {新米|しんまい} — novice; greenhorn — more casual, emphasizes inexperience
